sources.entry: twistel - Menu bar file converter: drag files, hold a key and drop them on a ring menu to convert images, audio, video and documents, compress, OCR, redact or sign PDFs, fully offline. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jonasnlt/twistel) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: twistel is a free, offline macOS menu bar app that converts, compresses, OCRs, redacts and signs files via a ring menu you open by holding a key while dragging files in the Finder.
summary.what_it_does: Drag one or more files in the Finder, hold a key, and a ring menu appears at the pointer; dropping files on an option creates a new result file next to the original. The Shift ring converts to formats the selection supports, the Command ring offers tools such as compress, crop, sign a PDF or recognize text, and the Control ring offers actions such as copy, copy path, checksum, move, AirDrop and share. Crop, rotate and compress have presets (aspect ratios, rotations, size limits, video resolutions). Supported conversions cover images, audio, video, documents, spreadsheets, presentations, subtitles and archives, and 42 tools are listed across images, video, audio and PDFs. Some tools rely on optional free helper programs (ffmpeg, LibreOffice, Ghostscript, qpdf, whisper.cpp, Poppler, unar) installed through Homebrew, which run in a network-blocking macOS sandbox. The app is in English and German.
use_cases: convert HEIC photos to JPG or PNG
compress a PDF or video under a size limit
extract text from scanned PDFs or images
convert documents or spreadsheets without uploading them
resize or crop images for social media
how_to_run: Download twistel-1.1.0.dmg from the Releases page
Drag twistel into Applications and start it from there
Approve the first start under System Settings › Privacy & Security (Open Anyway)
Optional: install Homebrew helpers, e.g. brew install ffmpeg
Create a finished release in dist/: ./scripts/release.sh
notable: Ring menu opened by holding a key during a Finder drag, with no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission needed
Network-free by design: release builds are checked for networking code and helper programs run in a sandbox that blocks network access
314 conversions and 42 tools across images, audio, video, documents, PDFs
Originals are never touched; results go to a temp folder and only move next to the original on success
Built on Satsuma by plyght (MIT) and licensed GPL-3.0
caveats: Apple silicon only and requires macOS 26 or later; Intel Macs are not supported
Not notarized by Apple, so the first start needs a manual override in System Settings
Personal project with no support and no schedule; pull requests are not accepted
